title: Topological sort
objective: Order tasks that depend on each other, so every task comes after what it needs.

sources.title: Cormen, Leiserson, Rivest and Stein, Introduction to Algorithms, 4th ed. (MIT Press, 2022): topological sort

simplifies: Every example here is possible to order. If tasks waited on each other in a loop, some would never become ready: Kahn's method would end with tasks left over, which is how it detects a cycle.

options.explanation: Right. They have no incoming arrows, so nothing must happen before them.

options.text: Those with the most arrows out
options.explanation: Arrows out don't matter; a task can start once nothing is waiting in front of it.
A task with an incoming arrow must wait for that task.

quiz.prompt: If two tasks each wait on the other, what happens?

options.text: Neither ever becomes ready, so no valid order exists
options.explanation: Right. A cycle makes ordering impossible; Kahn's method ends with tasks left over.

options.text: They run at the same time
options.explanation: In this model they can't: each needs the other finished first.

options.text: The one with the smaller name goes first
